**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity)**

- **Issue:** Section 11.1 binds Corio to a five-year initial term with automatic one-year renewals, and the only termination routes are non-renewal at expiry, material breach, or insolvency (11.2). Sections 3.x and 7 give only narrow refund-linked exits (acceptance-test failure, uncorrectable warranty breach). There is no customer termination-for-convenience right at all during the committed term — walk-away territory under T4C and short of the fallback.
- **Redline (validated, preferred position):** new Section 11.2 letting Corio terminate for convenience, in whole or in part, on 30 days' written notice, with no termination fee or penalty and a refund of prepaid fees allocable to the post-termination period.
- **Noted, not flagged:** Commerce One's non-renewal notice is 30 days rather than the preferred 90, but it is a mutual end-of-term non-renewal right rather than a mid-term vendor convenience exit, so it was left alone.
